title: Repair the shutdown callback lifetime fault
prompt:
Repair the C++ shutdown crash in this repository. This is an offline, deterministic incident reproduction; work only in the supplied workspace.

Start with the symbolized stack trace and captured lifecycle snapshot in `.protected/incident/`, then inspect the implementation. Treat `.protected/incident/` and `protected_tests/` as read-only evidence. The failure is in callback ownership during teardown, not in the event payload. Fix the implementation so a queued callback never dereferences a destroyed `Session` and the `EventLoop` does not extend a `Session`'s lifetime. Normal `Runtime` teardown must still drain pending completions while its session is alive. An explicit early `Runtime::stop()` must release the session immediately; any callback already queued at that point must safely become a no-op.

Make the required destruction dependency explicit and durable: the event loop must finish destruction before the session retained by `Runtime` is destroyed. Do not solve this with a global or static owner, a leaked allocation, a process-lifetime registry, or by suppressing shutdown draining. Keep the existing public API and audit messages. Do not add sleeps or timing assumptions.

Run `bash protected_tests/verify.sh` from the repository root to verify the repair.
